topic: Learning to swim at the city pool
passage: Last Sunday morning, my wife signed me up for a swimming class at the city pool. Although I had never learned to swim before, I agreed to try because I wanted to get fit and spend more time outside. At nine, I walked into the pool building and met the coach, a tall man with a kind smile. He asked me to warm up beside the pool and practice breathing slowly. At first, I felt nervous when I stepped into the cold water, and I held on to the edge. The coach showed me how to float on my back and kick my legs gently. I practiced for an hour, and I swallowed some water twice, but I did not give up. After the class, I cooled down in the warm shower and changed into dry clothes. My wife picked me up at the door and asked how I felt. I told her I felt tired but proud, because I had floated alone for ten seconds. We walked home, and I promised to practice again next Sunday. Learning to swim is hard at my age, but it showed me that it is never too late to start something new.
